the present study provides a simple and effective strategy for the preparation of TiO(,2)-Au composites, which is of great interest for a wide range of potential applications.

the use of hydrophobic TiO(2)nano-rods as a stabilizer for the generation of gold nanoparticles in organic media represents a unique approach for the preparation of TiO( 2)-stabilised Au nanoparticle composites.

the present study provides a new insight into the formation of Au nanoparticles and their composites with TiO(2), which is based on the use of titania-nanoparticle-assisted generation of Au nanoparticles at aqueous/organic interfaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that titania nanorods can be used to assist the reduction of gold ions at the aqueous/nonpola solvent interface and that this method can be extended to the synthesis of TiO2/Au composites.

the use of titania nanorods as a stabilizer and as a template for the generation of Au nanoparticles at the water/1-octanol interface provides a straightforward approach to the synthesis of TiO2/Au nanocomposites.

the use of TiO( 2) nanorod as a surfactant to assist the reduction of gold ions at aqueous/non-polar solvent interfaces provides an efficient method for the surfactants free synthesis of Au nanoparticles with tunability in size and composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
titania nanorods can be used as nanoreactors to generate metal nanoparticles in organic solvents.
the interfacial energy of the reaction medium can be tuned to promote the formation of metal nanoclusters and nanoparticles, which can be stabilized by titania nanorods.
titania nanorods can act as nanocatalysts in the generation of gold nanoparticles, which is of great interest in the context of nanocomposite synthesis and catalysis.
